## Results

- A 30-question statistics quiz sets each team's salary cap; teams then draft players in a silent auction and play a 2d6 dice-baseball tournament
- Dice tables built from real OBP, SLG and ERA: P(2d6 >= 6) x E[bases | hit] = 26/36 x 2.333 = 1.684 expected bases per plate appearance
- All 30 answer keys re-derived and verified
- Classroom-tested as the final-exam review in MA206, with submissions collected through Google Sheets

## The problem

Cumulative review before the term-end exam is usually passive and low-engagement.

## What I built

I built a Streamlit quiz that pays out a salary cap and writes results to Google Sheets, mapped real OBP, SLG and ERA onto 2d6 dice probability tables, and wrote a scouting guide around expected bases per plate appearance using the law of total expectation.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What it is for

Turns probability tables and expected value into resource-allocation decisions under a budget, which parallels analytic tradeoffs.
:::

## Tools

Python, Streamlit, pandas, gspread
